problem: Semantic exploration and object-goal navigation methods assume static scenes and lack persistent instance-level tracking, so they cannot maintain a map under semi-static changes (objects moved, removed, reintroduced) that are not observed continuously. Prior change-detection mapping (Khronos, Panoptic TSDF) is geometry-only or noise-sensitive, and DynaMem updates its map but cannot use semantics to search for unseen objects.
motivation: Home robots must keep a metric-semantic map that reflects the current world and find objects efficiently, like a person guessing where glasses were left. Changes are only seen when a region is revisited, so the robot needs a probabilistic belief about which objects are still where they were last seen, and it should act on that belief by revisiting stale areas and by using LLM commonsense to prioritise search regions.
key_idea: Track each object instance with a probabilistic stationarity score (LLM-derived static/dynamic prior plus Bayesian change detection) in an open-vocabulary 3D map, and turn the scores and LLM object-goal relevancies into a 2D exploration priority map from which waypoints are sampled for map maintenance or object search.
insight: Combining semantic and geometric similarity is necessary for robust instance re-identification: the ablation shows that each measure alone fails on some object pairs (different semantics only or different geometry only). Semantic checks are what allow change detection of small objects like a vase, which explains the large F1 gain over geometry-only Khronos on the cluttered apartment. Sensitivity analysis shows F1 varies at most ±7.0 over wide parameter ranges, and decaying stationarity of out-of-view objects is what drives revisits.
method: Object candidate extraction: SAM masks on RGB-D, CLIP features and class labels per mask, back-projected to point clouds (ConceptGraphs-style), with a distance cutoff; unmasked points go into a background point cloud.

Expected-view 2-step association: objects whose visible point fraction ≥ τ_expected are matched first by geometric similarity (assuming stationarity) plus semantic threshold, then remaining candidates by CLIP similarity verified with ICP RMSE; unmatched candidates become new objects.

Stationarity score update: per-object Bayesian belief over stationarity v and geometric change (following POCD), with an LLM static/dynamic class prior; out-of-view objects receive synthetic change so v decays faster for dynamic classes, stopping at the removal threshold θ_r.

Removal, reintroduction and translation: objects with v ≤ θ_r move to a missing library; objects in the missing library or with θ_r<v≤θ_t are re-identified against new objects appearing within a ±τ window of their disappearance using semantic-conditioned ICP, then merged.

Exploration priority map: sum of per-object Gaussian-smoothed occupancy shadows, with σ growing as stationarity falls, weighted by relevancy; for maintenance the relevancy is a normalized Beta(5,6) PDF of stationarity; for search it is an LLM 0-100 score of the target being near each object class.

Waypoint sampling and control: draw M candidate waypoints from the error between the priority map and the density of past waypoints, choose the candidate closest to the robot, then plan with A* and track with MPC.

setting.backbone: SAM + CLIP (frozen) for perception; an LLM (frozen, unspecified in the text) for stationarity priors and object relevancy
setting.observation: RGB-D (Orbbec Femto Bolt) with camera poses from VIO (HybVIO)
setting.action_space: 2D waypoints on the floor plane, executed with A* global planning and MPC
setting.simulator: InteriorAgent dataset (closed-loop simulation); Khronos dataset (offline mapping); real-world Hello Robot Stretch 3
setting.privileged: Camera poses are assumed known (from VIO); an optional prior map may be given. In the InteriorAgent object-goal navigation tests, the prior map is built by 15 min of frontier exploration.

numbers_note: No standard benchmark is used. Object-goal navigation results are on an author-designed InteriorAgent task set (60 tasks) and are printed as fractions (0.65 etc.). The real-world mapping tables (geometric and object accuracy, change detection efficiency) are not included as entries.
results: On the 60 InteriorAgent tasks, the method beats DynaMem in SR and SPL in every category (e.g., Known 0.65/0.62 vs 0.45/0.36, Moved 0.50/0.43 vs 0.25/0.24) and beats a random baseline. On Khronos, change-detection F1 is higher on both scenes (89.3 vs ≤50.2 apartment, 53.0 vs ≤39.4 office). In the real world it identifies 87.5% of additions and 100% of removals in the larger scene, and is ~14% faster than patrol in object search at equal success rate.
limitations: Uses only a 2D priority map for wheeled robots and assumes known camera poses from VIO
Real-world evaluation is small (8 search runs per method, 3 environments), and the InteriorAgent benchmark is custom-built with 60 tasks
Not designed for continuously dynamic objects, and the precision/recall trade-off depends on hand-tuned thresholds
